newsitem.title: USA: Dlr bolstered by rate rise, ends higher in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Dlr bolstered by rate rise, ends higher in U.S..

text.p: The dollar rose against most major currencies on Tuesday, bolstered by a rise in short-term interest rates by Federal Reserve policymakers and fresh signs Japan will maintain its current accomodative monetary policy.

At its regularly scheduled meeting, the Federal Open Market Committee boosted its overnight federal funds lending rate target for the first time since February 1, 1995 by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent.
The rise matched financial market expectations but caused the dollar to briefly spike lower then higher against the mark from its pre-announcement level in sporadic trade.
Soon after, the dollar stabilized still higher for the session but below earlier levels as U.S. stock and bond markets turned decidedly negative.

"The dollar is clearly the tail rather than the dog here. It's following the reaction in U.S. asset markets," said Ben Strauss, an assistant vice-president at Bank Julius Baer and Co. Strauss described dollar trade just after the Fed announcement as "very choppy".
The dollar rose to 1.6898/03 marks by the end of trade from 1.6870/80 at Tuesday's open and to 123.75/80 yen from 123.45/50.
The Dow Jones industrials and 30-year U.S. Treasury bond shed morning gains after the FOMC announcement and closed in negative territory, pulling the dollar from its session highs.
"The Fed rate hike was as expected and the currency market behaved as expected," said John Nelson, foreign exchange trading manager at ABN-AMRO Bank in Chicago.

"People initially bought dollars on the perception of higher U.S. interest rates, but upon further inspection most of the market had already priced in that move and, later, we moved with other U.S. asset markets," he added.

Earlier, the dollar rose against the yen after the Bank of Japan allowed the overnight call rate to dip to an average of 53 basis points from 57 on Monday. Comments from a top Japanese banker who said Japanese interest rates will remain low for some time also helped dollar/yen.

Shunsaku Hashimoto, head of the Federation of Bankers' Associations of Japan, said Japanese monetary policy would become more flexible in the second half of the fiscal year ending March 31, 1998. The comment caused the mark to surge against the yen, pulling dollar/yen higher as well.

In other trading, the dollar rose to 1.4640/50 Swiss francs from 1.4575/85 at the open and Canadian $1.3783/88 from C$1.3775/80. Sterling rose modestly after a sharp rally on Monday, closing at $1.6185/95 from $1.6165/75. The Australian dollar fell to $0.7831/36 from $0.7862/67.
